_comment: Shared tunables for gesture_meme.py (desktop) and app.js (browser). Edit values here, not in the code - both implementations load this file directly, so they can no longer drift out of sync. Ratios are normalized by hand/face scale so they hold regardless of distance from the camera. Angles are degrees.

smoothing._comment: voteTauMs/switchVoteThreshold replace the old 'N consecutive identical frames' debounce with a time-decayed vote, so one dissenting frame no longer resets progress and latency doesn't drift with fps. minScoreFloor/scoreMargin gate the scored gesture arbitration: below the floor, no hand shape is confident enough to call; between two candidates closer than the margin, the frame is reported as 'ambiguous' and cast as a non-vote so the display holds instead of flickering.

finger._comment: Per-finger extension score in [0,1], computed from hand WORLD landmarks (metric, perspective-corrected) rather than image landmarks - this is what makes a finger pointed straight at the camera still read as extended instead of foreshortening it past the old fixed 45-degree cliff. curl = summed bend angle across mcp-pip-dip-tip; reach = chord/arc ratio (foreshortening-robust). hysteresisHigh/Low latch the continuous score into a stable up/down boolean per finger, keyed by handedness, so a score hovering near the middle doesn't flap the boolean every frame. Tune against the live HUD.

thumb._comment: spread = thumb-tip to pinky-mcp distance / hand scale (world landmarks) - how far the thumb is abducted from a tucked fist. upAngleLoDeg/HiDeg score how close the thumb (mcp->tip, in IMAGE coordinates - direction only makes sense relative to the screen, not the hand's own 3D frame) points to straight up; this is the missing orientation test that let a thumbs-down read as thumbsUp before.

face._comment: Unchanged from before: yaw comes from MediaPipe's own facial transformation matrix, mouthOpen from lip landmark distance / face width.

hand._comment: All hand<->face and hand<->hand distances are 2D (image x/y only, dist2): hand-landmarker z is relative to that hand's own wrist and face-landmarker z is relative to the head, so mixing them across detectors adds noise, not signal. shhh vs oneFingerUp (professor cat) share one hand shape (index finger only extended) and are told apart by three continuous, scored features instead of one hard-cliff distance check: how close the tip is to the mouth (shhhDistLo/Hi), how level it is with the mouth (shhhVertOffsetLo/Hi, signed so a tip held below the mouth doesn't score as 'up' either), and how vertical the finger itself is (pointUpAngleLoDeg/HiDeg) - which is also what stops a sideways- or downward-pointing finger from reading as professor cat, a gap the original had no test for at all.

spin._comment: Unchanged from before (desktop-only; app.js has no optical flow / spin detection). See gesture_meme.py for the tuning history behind these numbers.
